A-1.title: Map the repository before building
A-1.what: Identify which documents and code are authoritative, what is current, and what is legacy or future.
A-1.why: Carbon cannot build safely if later work mistakes an old plan or future design for current truth.
A-1.changes: The team gets one bounded starting map for the build.
A-1.not_yet: This ticket does not implement Carbon behavior.

A0.title: Give each part of Carbon a clear home
A0.what: Create a stable software layout so scoring, hidden-test handling, submissions, results, and later services have separate owners.
A0.why: Clear boundaries reduce the chance that one module silently takes authority from another.
A0.changes: Later work can add behavior without inventing the software structure again.
A0.not_yet: A clean package layout proves no scientific behavior.

A1.title: Create a common automated test path
A1.what: Set up repeatable CPU tests and preserve the code-quality pipeline.
A1.why: Every later change needs the same basic engineering proof before it can be called complete.
A1.changes: Carbon gets a shared automated evidence lane for software changes.
A1.not_yet: Passing software tests does not prove scientific correctness or production readiness.

A2.title: Define what a participant is allowed to submit
A2.what: Create a strict, declarative strategy format and reject malformed submissions before anything executes.
A2.why: Participants need freedom to propose methods without receiving arbitrary execution authority.
A2.changes: Carbon can accept one bounded strategy object that later stages can rebuild and test.
A2.not_yet: This ticket does not train, rebuild, or grade a model.

A3.title: Make sure Carbon knows the exact exam it is running
A3.what: Give every Challenge an exact registered identity and refuse activation when the required identity or qualification does not match.
A3.why: The system must never grade against an ambiguous or substituted exam.
A3.changes: Later components can bind their work to one exact Challenge version and fail closed on a mismatch.
A3.not_yet: An identity check does not scientifically qualify the exam.

A4.title: Keep training, practice, and hidden testing separate
A4.what: Separate the random information used for different roles and test for accidental leakage between them.
A4.why: A hidden evaluation stops being meaningful if competitors can infer the official test material from training or practice.
A4.changes: Carbon has explicit separation and leakage guards for its different sources of randomness.
A4.not_yet: Random-seed separation alone does not prove the entire exam is free from information leakage.

A5.title: Make the scoring code execute fixed rules
A5.what: Build a bounded scoring engine that applies registered pass/fail and ranking rules to controlled test data.
A5.why: The evaluator should execute scientific policy that was defined in advance, not invent rules after seeing results.
A5.changes: Carbon has one place that can apply fixed eligibility and ranking rules to evidence.
A5.not_yet: This does not create a production-qualified exam or make scores comparable across different Challenges.

A6.title: Keep private evidence separate from public results
A6.what: Store useful internal result information while exposing only fields that are safe to publish.
A6.why: Carbon needs detailed evidence for review without leaking hidden tests or private information.
A6.changes: The system gains an explicit disclosure boundary between internal records and public projections.
A6.not_yet: This does not authorize public production publication.

A7.title: Track a submission from start to finish without mixing failure types
A7.what: Give submissions exact identity and lifecycle states, and distinguish scientific failure from infrastructure failure, cancellation, and refund handling.
A7.why: A broken machine, a failed model, and an economic refund are different events and need different records.
A7.changes: Carbon gets a bounded lifecycle for submissions and their terminal outcomes.
A7.not_yet: This does not implement treasury settlement, chain economics, or live payments.

A8.title: Test the evaluation lifecycle with a safe fake backend
A8.what: Run the official-shaped workflow against deterministic fixtures before real training or participant code exists.
A8.why: Carbon needs to prove the pieces connect correctly before putting real execution behind them.
A8.changes: The team can exercise the lifecycle end to end with controlled local behavior.
A8.not_yet: This does not run real training, arbitrary code, production sandboxes, or emissions.

A9.title: Give researchers a small, stable way to interact with Carbon
A9.what: Expose a fixed local interface for Challenge information, practice scaffolding, validation, resource estimates, submission, and result lookup.
A9.why: Researchers need a stable interface before Carbon adds remote networking or richer research services.
A9.changes: Carbon gets a bounded participant-facing interface that later network layers can wrap.
A9.not_yet: This does not add authentication, remote transport, production quotas, or production content.

A10.title: Publish rankings without leaking the hidden exam
A10.what: Create a public leaderboard view that exposes only approved result fields.
A10.why: A leaderboard should show useful ranking information without exposing private evidence or pretending to be a frontier decision.
A10.changes: Carbon can publish a bounded public ranking projection.
A10.not_yet: This does not prove a scientific frontier advance or qualify a product.

A11.title: Make failures and system behavior observable without exposing protected data
A11.what: Record structured runtime state, failure categories, retry information, environment information, and safe evidence identifiers.
A11.why: Operators need enough information to diagnose the system while the hidden exam stays hidden.
A11.changes: Carbon gets a bounded logging and metrics contract for review and operations.
A11.not_yet: This does not grant access to protected cases or establish production operations.

A12.title: Test the boundaries themselves and close the foundation wave
A12.what: Check that forbidden cross-boundary behavior stays forbidden, not just that the happy path works.
A12.why: Individual features can pass while the system still violates a trust boundary.
A12.changes: Carbon gets a bounded closeout proof that the Wave A software boundaries hold in the recorded scope.
A12.not_yet: Wave A closeout does not advance scientific, security, network, commercial, or production qualification.
